criteria.name: Q1 Quality attributes
criteria.reasoning: Two relevant attributes justified from lunch-peak. Performance scenario complete and measurable. Availability scenario has six parts but response measure is vague and not measurable.

evidence.quote: the system should stay up most of the time.

criteria.name: Q2 Architectural style
criteria.reasoning: Clear modular-monolith recommendation. Two scenario-specific trade-offs: 5-person team overhead and single-VM plus deployment downtime. Downside acknowledged.

evidence.quote: modules cannot be scaled independently, and a bug in one module can still crash

criteria.name: Q3 Availability calculation
criteria.reasoning: Parts (a) 99.30% and (b) 5.0 hours correct with working. Part (c) uses payment-only availability, omits other components; correct is ~99.80% and ~1.5h downtime.

evidence.quote: So the new availability of placing an order is 99.9975%

criteria.name: Q4 Resilience pattern
criteria.reasoning: Circuit Breaker appropriate, mechanism correctly explained and applied to 25-min outage. No explicit drawback or tuning trade-off discussed.

evidence.quote: After a wait period the breaker goes Half-Open and lets a few trial calls through.

criteria.name: Q5 Consistency and availability
criteria.reasoning: Both AP for menus and CP for payments choices reasonable with techniques. CAP misused: partition tolerance cannot be given up.

evidence.quote: so for payments we choose consistency and availability and give up partition tolerance.

criteria.name: Q6 Architecture decision record
criteria.reasoning: Context and Decision specific to outlet notification. Consequences list only positives; no negative consequence like ops complexity or ordering.

evidence.quote: The queue also smooths the lunch peak because the workers process orders at a steady rate.

criteria.name: Communication and format
criteria.reasoning: Headings and IEEE references present, writing clear, but Q2 ~182 words exceeds 150-word limit.

evidence.quote: I recommend against a full microservices rewrite for the next 12 months.

technical_issues.issue: Part (c) incorrect: end-to-end availability must multiply 0.9995x0.999x0.9995x0.999975=~99.80%, downtime ~1.5h, not 99.9975% / 0.018h.
CAP statement incorrect; partitioned system must tolerate partitions and trades C vs A. Idempotency key does not provide consistency.
Availability response measure not measurable, no target percentage/time.

overall: Mostly strong analysis with correct series method but Q3c miscalculation, CAP error, missing measurable and ADR negative.

feedback.summary: You produced mostly strong, scenario-grounded analysis with clear strengths in Q2 style and Q3 working. To reach Excellent, make your measures measurable, fix your Q3c chain calculation, correct CAP, and add drawback and negative consequence discussion.
next_steps: Add a measurable target to your Q1 availability response measure and recalculate Q3c by multiplying all four components.
Correct your Q5 CAP explanation to show partition tolerance is mandatory and check your consistency techniques.
Add an explicit Q4 tuning drawback and a Q6 negative consequence, and trim Q2 to under 150 words.

criteria.C1: Well done choosing two relevant attributes with lunch-peak justification, your performance scenario was complete and measurable. For Excellent, make your availability response measure measurable by adding a specific target percentage or time instead of 'stay up most of the time'.
criteria.C2: Excellent work in Question 2 recommending a modular monolith with two scenario-specific trade-offs on your 5-person team and single-VM downtime. You acknowledged the downside that modules cannot scale independently and a bug can crash, keep this specificity.
criteria.C3: Well done showing working for Q3a 99.30% and Q3b 5.0 hours correctly in Question 3. For Excellent, fix Q3c by multiplying all components, not payment-only 99.9975%, to get about 99.80% and about 1.5h downtime.
criteria.C4: Well done naming Circuit Breaker in Question 4 and correctly explaining Half-Open trial calls applied to the 25-min outage. For Excellent, add one explicit drawback or tuning consideration such as threshold, timeout or fallback trade-off.
criteria.C5: Well done choosing AP for menus and CP for payments with concrete techniques in Question 5. For Excellent, correct CAP to state a partitioned system must tolerate partitions and trades C vs A, so you cannot give up partition tolerance for payments.
criteria.C6: Well done with specific Context and Decision on outlet notification and queue smoothing the lunch peak in Question 6. For Excellent, add at least one negative consequence such as ops complexity, ordering or debugging cost alongside positives.
criteria.C7: Well done using required headings, clear writing and IEEE references. For Excellent, keep every answer within 150 words, especially Q2 which exceeded at about 182 words, and ensure precise terminology and citation format.
